deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The neighbouring pages fix a von Neumann algebra 𝒜 on H with a faithful normal semifinite trace T. 𝔞 and 𝔟 are two-sided ideals: 𝔞 is most likely the trace class and 𝔟 a closure of it, i.e. T-compact or T-measurable operators. For A ≥ 0, μ_A is the spectral distribution measure T∘E_A. φ_A(t) is the decreasing rearrangement of A, i.e. its generalized singular value function. Prop. 6 on the previous page gives the min-max formulas φ_{|A|}(t) = inf_{T(E)<t} ‖A(1−E)‖.

Prop. 7. For A ∈ 𝔟, μ_{|A|} = μ_{|A*|}, equivalently φ_{|A|} = φ_{|A*|}.
- Since φ_{|A|²} = φ_{A*A} and φ_{|A*|²} = φ_{AA*}, it suffices to show φ_{A*A} = φ_{AA*}.
- By the continuity of A ↦ φ_{|A|}(t) on 𝔟 (Cor. 4, previous page), one may restrict to A ∈ 𝔞.
- Then μ_{AA*} and μ_{A*A} are measures with compact support on ℝ⁺. Such measures are determined by their moments.
- The moments are equal: T((AA*)^p) = T((A*A)^p), which follows from T(RS) = T(SR).
- Consequently every quantity defined from φ (Φ, ψ, etc.) is the same for |A| and |A*|.

No. 6, the determinant. For suitable A he defines Δ(A) = exp ∫_0^{T(1)} log φ_{|A|}(t) dt.
- (a) If T is finite, Δ is defined on all of 𝒜, with 0 ≤ Δ < ∞ and Δ(λA) = |λ|^{T(1)} Δ(A). This is exactly the Fuglede–Kadison determinant, written as the geometric mean of the generalized s-numbers.
- (b) If T is infinite, he considers A = λ1 + B with B ∈ 𝔟. The next page gives the trichotomy: Δ = 0 if |λ| < 1, Δ = +∞ if |λ| > 1, and if |λ| = 1 then Δ < ∞ iff B ∈ 𝔞.
- He then proves multiplicativity, Δ(A*) = Δ(A) and Δ(1) = 1 on 1 + 𝔞. This is done by reducing to the finite corner E𝒜E, where E is the support projection of B. In effect this gives a Fredholm-type determinant for 1 + trace-class in a semifinite algebra.

Purpose. These notes develop a theory of 'rearrangements' and singular numbers in semifinite von Neumann algebras. It is the material behind Grothendieck's Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 113 (1955) on rearrangements and convexity inequalities, extended here to determinants.
errors: Prop. 7 proof: for an infinite trace, μ_{A*A} may have infinite mass at 0. 'Measures with compact support on R+' and moment p = 0 then only make sense on (0,∞) (or with the mass at 0 handled separately). Using p ≥ 1 on (0,∞) suffices, so this is minor.

Definition (1) applied directly with T infinite to A = 1+B: φ_{|A|}(t) is the rearrangement of the whole operator, so it is ≥ 1 for all t. The spectral part of |1+B| below 1 is lost, and the formula would then give Δ(1+B) ≥ 1 always. The integral formula is therefore not literally the right definition in the infinite case.
  - The next page in effect repairs this by setting Δ(1+A) = Δ_E(1_E+A_E) in the finite corner E𝒜E.
  - The stated criterion 'Δ < ∞ iff B ∈ 𝔞' would, under the naive formula, only test the positive part of |1+B|−1.

ideas.what: Equality of singular value functions of A and A* (φ_{|A|} = φ_{|A*|}) in a semifinite von Neumann algebra, proved via moments and the trace property
Determinant as exp ∫ log of the decreasing rearrangement of |A|
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison determinant Δ(A) = exp ∫ log μ_t(A) dt
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fuglede–Kadison (1952) for the determinant; the s-number formula to Fack–Kosaki (1986)
ideas.where_published: unsure (Bourbaki exp. 113 treats rearrangements; whether it treats determinants is unknown to me)

ideas.what: Determinant for λ1+B in a semifinite algebra with infinite trace: 0/∞ trichotomy in |λ|, finiteness iff B trace class, multiplicativity on 1+𝔞 via reduction to a finite corner
ideas.modern_name: Fuglede–Kadison/Fredholm determinant on 1 + L¹(𝒜,τ) for semifinite 𝒜
ideas.usually_credited_to: later work, e.g. de la Harpe–Skandalis (1984), L. G. Brown (1986, Lidskii theorem in type II)

missed.claim: In 1953 Grothendieck expresses the Fuglede–Kadison determinant through generalized singular numbers, Δ(A) = exp∫_0^{T(1)} log φ_{|A|}. In the literature this formula is usually attributed to Fack–Kosaki (1986).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical priority for the s-number description of the FK determinant. This is used in L²-invariants and Brown measure theory.

missed.claim: He extends the determinant to 1 + trace class in a semifinite algebra with infinite trace. The extension comes with the |λ| trichotomy and multiplicativity, decades before standard treatments of semifinite Fredholm determinants.
missed.quote: Si T est infinie, ... A = λ1 + B (B ∈ 𝔟)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would be early, uncredited work on semifinite Fredholm determinants. They are relevant to spectral flow and Breuer–Fredholm theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Prop. 7 is routine. The determinant section anticipates the Fack–Kosaki s-number formula for the FK determinant and its semifinite extension. However, Grothendieck's rearrangement work is partly published (Bourbaki 1955), and the FK determinant itself predates these notes, so the novelty is a priority detail.
transcription_corrections: 'μ' on the first lines is Grothendieck's measure notation μ_{|A|}; the equivalence is with φ_{|A|} = φ_{|A*|}.
In 'Δ(A) = ... exp' the crossed-out word is replaced by 'exp' written above it.
The final line is likely '(B ∈ 𝔞, B hermitien)' or similar, not '(B ∈ 𝔟, B ...)'.
